title: Add MCP health and stats introspection tools
description:
Problem: external agents currently have no first-class MCP tool for checking MemorySmith service readiness, stats, or bounded operational diagnostics. The app already exposes `/health`, `/api/stats`, and `/api/diagnostics` through `HealthController`, `StatsController`, and `DiagnosticsController`, and the wiki documents those surfaces, but MCP callers must infer system state indirectly from search behavior and tool failures. That makes it harder for external agents to distinguish an empty result set from a degraded embedding provider, disabled feature surface, or broader runtime issue.

Evidence from 2026-05-26 audit:
- `MemorySmith.App/Controllers/HealthController.cs`, `StatsController.cs`, and `DiagnosticsController.cs` already expose health/diagnostic information over HTTP.
- `MemorySmith.App/Services/OperationalDiagnosticsService.cs` builds the redacted operational snapshot behind those surfaces.
- `Data/Pages/features/health-and-diagnostics.md` and `README.md` document the health/stats endpoints for humans, but `Data/Tasks` contains no MCP-facing task for exposing an equivalent bounded read-only surface to agents.

Desired outcome: external MCP agents can query a small, explicit health/stats surface before or after retrieval work without scraping human-oriented pages or guessing from downstream failures.

Scope:
- In scope: one or more read-only MCP tools that expose bounded health, stats, and safe operational-diagnostics summaries appropriate for agent consumption.
- In scope: defining the authorization contract, redaction boundaries, and output shape for those tools.
- Out of scope: exposing secrets, raw logs, or full admin-only diagnostics dumps without redaction.

Acceptance criteria:
- MCP exposes a bounded read-only health/stats surface backed by the existing runtime services.
- The tool output clearly distinguishes readiness, counts/activity, and any degraded-provider or diagnostics summary fields that are safe to expose.
- The authorization contract is explicit and tested.
- Documentation explains when agents should use the MCP health/stats tools versus the existing UI/REST surfaces.

Validation:
- Add focused tests for the new MCP tool surface and authorization behavior.
- Run the affected MCP/diagnostics test slice.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task creation/update.

comments.body: Created during Claude benchmark triage after verifying that MemorySmith already has human/REST health and stats surfaces but no equivalent MCP tool for external agents.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
## Council Review — MCP Health Tool: Scope, Auth, and Minimum Viable Shape

**Context:** Three benchmark sessions from an external Claude agent highlighted the inability to detect service degradation (ONNX availability, write-path state, source-bundle auth readiness) without making a tool call and observing its behavior. REST endpoints `/health`, `/api/stats`, and `/api/diagnostics` exist; no MCP equivalent does. Evidence: provider metadata is already embedded in every search result envelope (`provider.available`, `provider.mode`, `provider.reason`, model path), showing the runtime already tracks this state.

**Assumptions:**
- `[assumption]` A read-only MCP health tool would satisfy `View` permission — no reason to gate diagnostic visibility at `Edit` or higher.
- `[assumption]` The primary consumer is an external LLM agent that cannot make raw HTTP calls to `/api/diagnostics` and needs the same information surfaced through the MCP JSON-RPC path.
- `[assumption]` The existing `OperationalDiagnosticsService` already computes the relevant fields; this task is primarily a thin MCP handler over an existing service.

---

### The Advocate *(confidence: 86%)*
> **Position:** A minimal tool returning ONNX status, record count, and task-store health covers the highest-value cases with almost no implementation risk.

The most common reason an agent needs health data is to decide whether to attempt a source-bundle call (requires ONNX + source resolution) or whether search results can be trusted (requires ONNX available). The `provider` block in every search result already exposes this, but only as a side effect of running a search. A dedicated `memorysmith_health` tool returning `{ onnxAvailable, onnxMode, memoryCount, taskStoreHealthy, lastMaintenanceRun, varResolverHealthy }` in a single call would let agents preflight without making a throwaway search. The implementation sketches itself: call `OperationalDiagnosticsService.GetSummaryAsync()`, redact sensitive paths, return a fixed-shape JSON envelope. No new state required.

### The Devil's Advocate *(confidence: 60%)*
> **Position:** Agents that need health information should design their workflows to infer it from existing tool outputs rather than requiring a dedicated health tool.

Every search result already includes `provider.available`, `provider.mode`, and `provider.reason`. `context_pack` returns `warnings[]` that capture resolution failures. Task list/get calls will fail or return empty if the task store is unhealthy. A dedicated health tool adds a fixed API surface that must be maintained in sync with the actual service state — if `OperationalDiagnosticsService` changes, the health tool output schema drifts. The agent skill document can instead instruct agents to infer health from the provider block in their first search result, which is already guaranteed to be accurate because it comes from the live execution path.

### The Pragmatist *(confidence: 82%)*
> **Position:** Both approaches are valid; the difference is latency and intent clarity. Implement a minimal health tool but scope it tightly to avoid creating a second diagnostics surface that needs independent maintenance.

Recommended shape: one tool, `memorysmith_health`, returning a flat JSON object with five to eight fields. No pagination, no filters, no format param. Fields: `onnxAvailable` (bool), `onnxMode` (string: "onnx-embedding" or "fallback"), `memoryCount` (int), `pageCount` (int), `taskStoreHealthy` (bool), `lastMaintenanceRunUtc` (ISO-8601 or null), `varResolverHealthy` (bool). Auth: View. This is narrower than `/api/diagnostics` (no log data, no path details, no sensitive config), so it does not create a new security boundary to manage. Document in `features/api-and-mcp` that agents should call this first when planning source-bundle workflows.

---

### Open Questions
- [ ] Does `OperationalDiagnosticsService` already expose task-store and var-resolver health as distinct fields, or would these need to be added? If they need to be added, scope the task accordingly.
- [ ] Should `memorysmith_health` also report whether the MCP write path is currently in bootstrap-compatibility mode? Given TSK-0183's findings, this would be the single most useful diagnostic for external agents.

### Confidence Summary
| Dimension | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Gap is real | 92% | Confirmed across all three benchmark sessions; no MCP equivalent to /health exists |
| Implementation effort is low | 85% | Provider metadata already emitted per-search; OperationalDiagnosticsService exists |
| Scope creep risk | 40% | Risk is low if the tool is spec'd as a fixed flat envelope from day one |
